title: Embryo Similarities
seo_title: Grade 8 Embryo Similarities Worksheets: Comparing Embryos to Find Evolutionary Relationships
standard_text: Analyze displays of pictorial data to compare patterns of similarities in the embryological development across multiple species to identify relationships not evident in the fully formed anatomy.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on embryo similarities (NGSS MS-LS4-3): shared structures in early vertebrate embryos, what they become, and using embryo data to infer how closely species are related. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Embryos that stay alike longer are closer relatives.
key_sub: Early vertebrate embryos share a tail and gill-like pouches. Comparing development reveals relationships adults hide.
body_html:
How to think about it

Early embryos of vertebrates look surprisingly alike. They share a tail, pharyngeal pouches (gill-like folds) and a notochord.

As development continues, the embryos become different. The same early structure can become different parts: pharyngeal pouches become gills in fish but parts of the ear and throat in humans.

The longer two species' embryos stay alike, the more closely related they are. Embryos can show relationships that adult bodies hide.

Example

Human embryos look like chimpanzee embryos until late and like fish embryos only early. Closer relative?

Longer similarity = closer.

Answer: the chimpanzee

Example

What do pharyngeal pouches become in a fish?

Same start, different end.

Answer: gills

Common mistakes

  • Thinking human embryos have working gills.
  • Thinking embryos that look alike are the same species.
  • Thinking adult appearance always shows relationships best.

faq.q: Why do embryos of different animals look alike?
faq.a: They inherited the same early developmental plan from a common ancestor.
No. They have pharyngeal pouches, which become parts of the ear, throat and jaw, while in fish the same pouches become gills.

faq.q: How can embryos show how closely species are related?
faq.a: Species whose embryos stay similar until later stages of development are usually more closely related.
